## `SayHandle`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Satone.Say.SayHandle` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core` · mod API

What `Satone.Say` hands back: the line's id, whether it has finished, how it finished, and a way to take it out of the queue again.

`Satone.Say` returns as soon as the line is queued - the speaking itself takes seconds and belongs to the game's own scenario reader. Wait for it with [`SayHandle.Completion`](#sayhandle--completion), or poll [`SayHandle.IsCompleted`](#sayhandle--iscompleted) from a frame loop.

[`SayHandle.Completion`](#sayhandle--completion) is completed on Unity's main thread, so a synchronous continuation runs there; an `await` without a synchronisation context resumes on a thread-pool thread, and anything it does with the engine has to marshal back itself.

<a id="sayhandle--ctor"></a>

### `SayHandle(SayLine line, Func<SayLine, bool> cancel = null)`

Creates a handle for a line.

**Parameters**

- `line`: The line. Required.
- `cancel`: What to call when the caller cancels: it should take the line out of the queue and return true when it did. Null makes [`SayHandle.Cancel`](#sayhandle--cancel) always answer false.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentNullException`: `line` is null.

<a id="sayhandle--completion"></a>

Takes the line out of the queue if it has not started yet.

**Returns:** True when it was still waiting and is now cancelled. False when it has already started, already finished, or was never queued - the game's scenario reader owns a line it has begun, and stopping that mid-sentence is not this API's job.

<a id="sayhandle--complete"></a>

Records the outcome and releases anything waiting on [`SayHandle.Completion`](#sayhandle--completion). Called by the feature that owns the queue; the second call is ignored, so a line that both timed out and then ended is reported once.

**Parameters**

- `outcome`: How it finished.
- `detail`: Evidence, for the log. Null becomes empty.

**Returns:** True when this call was the one that completed the handle.

## `SayIdGenerator`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Satone.Say.SayIdGenerator` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Hands out the ids one `Satone.Say` line needs: a number, and from it the scenario group id, the localization row id, the generated voice name and the episode number.

Monotonic and unique for the lifetime of the process. That is the whole contract: the ids end up as keys in the game's master data next to its own 1381 rows, and a repeat would make one line overwrite another's text or clip.

The episode number matters as much as the id. The game finds a scenario group by `(ScenarioType, EpisodeNumber)` in several places (for example `FacilityVoiceTextScenario.StartScenario`), so a Say line must never land on an episode number one of the game's own `MotionScenario` groups uses - they run 1..29 in v1.17.2, and [`SayIdGenerator.FirstEpisode`](#sayidgenerator--firstepisode) starts far above them.

## `SayOutcome`

enum · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Satone.Say.SayOutcome` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core` · mod API

How a `Satone.Say` line ended.

| Name | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <a id="sayoutcome--pending"></a>`Pending` | 0 | Still queued or still being spoken. |
| <a id="sayoutcome--spoken"></a>`Spoken` | 1 | The game's scenario reader played the line and its `EndStory` was observed: voice, mouth, motion and timing were all the game's own. |
| <a id="sayoutcome--fellback"></a>`FellBack` | 2 | The scenario path was not available in time, so the line was spoken voice only: the clip was played through `HeroineService.PlayVoice` and her mouth moves, but the scenario motion and the game's text box do not happen, and nothing else draws the text (it is only in the console's `SAY` line). A line without a voice is only in the log. |
| <a id="sayoutcome--cancelled"></a>`Cancelled` | 3 | The caller cancelled it before it started. |
| <a id="sayoutcome--rejected"></a>`Rejected` | 4 | It was never accepted: bad request, feature off, or the queue was full. |
| <a id="sayoutcome--timedout"></a>`TimedOut` | 5 | It started but the game never reported the scenario ending, so the queue gave up on it rather than blocking every later line. |

## `SayQueue`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Satone.Say.SayQueue` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

The waiting room for `Satone.Say` lines: first in, first out, one line speaking at a time, and a policy for what to do when the game is busy with a scenario of its own.

Time is a parameter, never a field: every method takes `nowSeconds` on whatever clock the caller uses (`Time.unscaledTime` in the game, plain numbers in the tests). That is what makes the whole policy testable off-engine.

**The policy.** [`SayQueue.Next`](#sayqueue--next) is asked once a frame with "can a scenario start right now?".

1. A line is already speaking: nothing happens until its scenario ends ([`SayQueue.Complete`](#sayqueue--complete)) - unless it has been speaking for longer than [`SayQueue.ActiveTimeoutSeconds`](#sayqueue--activetimeoutseconds), in which case it is abandoned so one lost end event cannot wedge the queue for the rest of the session.
2. Nothing is speaking and the game can start one: the head line starts.
3. The game is busy and the head has waited longer than [`SayQueue.MaxWaitSeconds`](#sayqueue--maxwaitseconds): with [`SayQueue.FallbackWhenBusy`](#sayqueue--fallbackwhenbusy) it is handed back for the simple voice-plus-subtitle path; without it, it keeps waiting.

<a id="sayqueue--ctor"></a>

### `SayQueue(int capacity = 8, double maxWaitSeconds = 10.0, bool fallbackWhenBusy = true, double activeTimeoutSeconds = 120.0)`

Creates a queue.

**Parameters**

- `capacity`: How many lines may wait; values below 1 are raised to 1.
- `maxWaitSeconds`: How long a line waits for the game before [`SayStepKind.Fallback`](#saystepkind--fallback); values below 0 are raised to 0.
- `fallbackWhenBusy`: False to keep waiting for the scenario path however long the game stays busy.
- `activeTimeoutSeconds`: How long a speaking line may run before it is abandoned; values below 1 are raised to 1.

<a id="sayqueue--defaultactivetimeoutseconds"></a>

## `SayRequest`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Satone.Say.SayRequest` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core` · mod API

One brand-new line for Satone to speak: the text, the languages it exists in, the clip that speaks it and the expression, motion and gaze it is performed with.

Unity-free on purpose. The adapter (`SatoneSayFeature`) turns this into the game's own master-data rows and hands them to `ScenarioReader`; everything expressible without touching the engine - validation, id generation, queueing - lives here and is unit-tested.

**Which column gets which text.** [`SayRequest.Text`](#sayrequest--text) fills every language column of the game's localization row except Japanese, which takes [`SayRequest.TextJa`](#sayrequest--textja) (falling back to [`SayRequest.Text`](#sayrequest--text)). The game shows whichever column matches the player's language, so a caller that only has English still gets a line on screen in any language. [`SayRequest.Texts`](#sayrequest--texts) is separate: it is this line's own text table, and it is the only way to give the line a text in a language the game has no column for - a language a content pack declares. While the player has such a language chosen, the game's own text box asks the text seam for this row and shows that entry (or the language's declared fallback).

<a id="sayrequest--defaultlookseconds"></a>

### `const float DefaultLookSeconds = 0.6f`

Seconds the gaze tween takes when [`SayRequest.LookScale`](#sayrequest--lookscale) is set.

<a id="sayrequest--maxtextlength"></a>

### `const int MaxTextLength = 500`

Longest text a single line may carry, in characters.

The story UI types the text out one character at a time and the reader waits for it, so a runaway LLM answer would hold the scenario open for minutes. Anything longer is refused with a reason rather than silently truncated.

An empty text table, so callers never have to allocate one.

How long the gaze turn takes, in seconds. Ignored when [`SayRequest.LookScale`](#sayrequest--lookscale) is null.

<a id="sayrequest--motion"></a>

Body-motion name, alias or id for the Satone table (`wild001_good`, or its id `61`). Null leaves her motion alone.

<a id="sayrequest--movemouth"></a>

True to run the mouth-talk animation while the clip plays (the game's `isMoveMouse` on a `VoiceText` row). Ignored for a text-only line.

<a id="sayrequest--normalizedlanguage"></a>

What Satone says, in [`SayRequest.Language`](#sayrequest--language). Required; blank is refused.

<a id="sayrequest--textja"></a>

### `string TextJa { get; init; }`

The Japanese column of the game's row. Null means "use [`SayRequest.Text`](#sayrequest--text)", which is what a mod with no translation should do - the line is then the same in every language.

<a id="sayrequest--texts"></a>

### `IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> Texts { get; init; }`

Per-language texts, keyed by language code (`ja`, or a code a pack declares). They are served through a registered [`ISubtitleSource`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Subtitles.md#isubtitlesource): while the player has a pack language chosen, the game's text box shows this line in that language. Null or empty means "only what the game's own columns hold".

The voice clip name to speak, e.g. `Voice_CWY_Test`. Must satisfy [`VoiceNameRules.Pattern`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Voice.md#voicenamerules--pattern). Null or empty means a text-only line: the game shows the text and does not move her mouth.

Keys are normalised; an explicit entry in [`SayRequest.Texts`](#sayrequest--texts) always wins.

**Returns:** A detached, ordinal-keyed table. Never null.

## `SayStepKind`

enum · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Satone.Say.SayStepKind` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

What [`SayQueue.Next`](#sayqueue--next) wants the caller to do this frame.

| Name | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <a id="saystepkind--idle"></a>`Idle` | 0 | Nothing to do. |
| <a id="saystepkind--start"></a>`Start` | 1 | Start this line through the game's scenario reader. |
| <a id="saystepkind--fallback"></a>`Fallback` | 2 | Speak this line the simple way: it waited longer than the queue's patience while the game was busy. |
| <a id="saystepkind--abandon"></a>`Abandon` | 3 | Give up on the active line: the game never reported its scenario ending. |
